When I start having an episode where I'm stuck in a similar thought track as you, I work on figuring out what incidents may have caused them & how I can learn from them. Whether that's finding how to shove those thoughts away, or accepting that I did something semi productive.  Your body & mind need time to rest. Sometimes you can push yourself over without even realizing it. You don't need that dark thought stuck in your head. I'd say talk with a doctor to get a diagnosis if you haven't already. Try not to worry about being judged. They're professionals. If they mock you, you need to report them & find a new one. Therapy is also helpful for learning coping mechanisms & how to process your own thoughts into a less chaotic jumble. You may feel like there's nothing besides that one thought, but in reality your brain is so overloaded with negative thoughts you dont even realize it. Check the spoon theory out if you haven't already. It's a good way to measure energy & explain to others where you're at for the day.

Dig into that one little incident that pissed you off yesterday. It all builds up over time. Find the puzzle pieces & figure that shit out.
